name: Godot
use: The game engine, built in demos/godot from its release; the licence is that of what the build compiles, and its COPYRIGHT.txt names the licence of each third-party library the release carries
licence: MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSL-1.0 AND FTL AND Zlib AND Unlicense

name: Dolly's Lantern Drift
use: The Godot project of Dolly's showcase game (demos/godot/lantern-drift), which Godot's editor imports and exports in its package

name: Dolly's Voxel Flyover
use: The Godot project of Voxel Flyover (demos/godot/voxel-flyover), a flight over a planet its shaders compute, which Godot's editor imports and exports in its package

name: Dolly's Airtime in Godot
use: The Godot project of Airtime: Foundry (demos/godot/airtime), bhop's strafe trials on Airtime's movement, which Godot's editor imports and exports in its package

name: Tint
use: Dawn's WebGPU shader compiler: its SPIR-V reader and WGSL writer translate Godot's shaders for gpu@0 (demos/godot, spirv-wgsl)

name: SPIRV-Tools
use: SPIR-V passes before Tint reads Godot's shaders (demos/godot, spirv-wgsl)

name: SPIRV-Headers
use: SPIR-V's grammar and headers, for SPIRV-Tools and Tint (demos/godot, spirv-wgsl)

name: Truck Town
use: The demo projects' vehicle physics demo, exported by Godot's editor in demos/godot; its README credits the models and the ambient sounds

name: Dodge the Creeps
use: The game of Godot's first 2D tutorial, from the demo projects' release, exported by Godot's editor in demos/godot; its README credits the music
licence: MIT AND CC-BY-3.0 AND CC0-1.0 AND OFL-1.1
